status_summary: On 2025-01-29 FCC Chairman Brendan Carr asked the Enforcement Bureau to look into whether underwriting announcements by NPR and PBS member stations comply with the ban on commercial advertising by noncommercial educational (NCE) stations; Current corrected its headline to say the letter requested rather than opened an investigation, and TV Technology reported that the letter noted the stations' licenses limit them to NCE operation. No outcome of that review (inquiry letters, fines or consent decrees), no presidential instruction to the FCC, and no order or rulemaking changing the NCE status, reserved-band access or fee exemption of NPR- or PBS-affiliated stations was found. Federal Register queries of FCC documents since 2025-01-20 for underwriting and for public broadcasting returned only unrelated items, and Current's site search showed no 2026 FCC underwriting item. A 2026-06-25 final rule limiting applications for NCE reserved-band FM translators does not mention NPR, PBS or network affiliation. Executive Order 14290 (2025-05-01) addressed federal funding, not FCC status; Judge Randolph Moss (D.D.C., National Public Radio, Inc. v. Trump, No. 1:25-cv-01674) permanently enjoined agencies from implementing it on 2026-03-31, and the Corporation for Public Broadcasting has dissolved.

timeline.event: Chairman Carr sends letters to NPR and PBS asking the Enforcement Bureau to review whether underwriting by member stations violates the ban on advertising by NCE stations; Current corrected its report to say he requested the review and that an investigation was not confirmed. TV Technology reports the letter also noted that the roughly 1,500 member stations' authorizations limit them to NCE operation.
Executive Order 14290 directs the CPB board and federal agencies to end funding for NPR and PBS; its text as summarized by the Federal Register contains no instruction to the FCC on NCE designation.

Judge Randolph Moss (D.D.C.) rules in National Public Radio, Inc. v. Trump (No. 1:25-cv-01674) that challenged sections of Executive Order 14290 discriminate by viewpoint under the First Amendment, bars the agency defendants from implementing or enforcing them, and finds claims about the Corporation for Public Broadcasting moot because it has dissolved; a partial final judgment follows on 2026-04-23. The case summary does not mention the FCC.

FCC final rule (91 FR 38304, MB Docket 26-20, effective 2026-07-27) limits each applicant to ten applications in the 2026 NCE reserved-band FM translator window and limits eligibility to licensees of existing NCE FM, noncommercial AM or LPFM stations; it does not mention NPR, PBS or network affiliation.

title: Remove NPR- and PBS-affiliated stations from noncommercial educational (NCE) status
uncertainties: The stage is a judgment: the only FCC action found is a request for an underwriting-compliance review, which is related to NCE rules but does not change NCE status, so not_started is a defensible alternative. The absence finding rests on Federal Register API queries of FCC documents (underwriting: 2 unrelated results; public broadcasting: 3 results, one an unrelated Savannah TV channel proposal), a prior scan of FCC NCE documents (first 40 of 43 read), Current.org site searches (no 2026 FCC underwriting item), and four web searches that returned only January 2025 coverage. The FCC's own site returned HTTP 403, so FCC Enforcement Bureau letters or consent decrees not reflected in the Federal Register or trade press could have been missed. The letter itself was not opened. The earlier claim of a March 2025 Senate subcommittee inquiry rested on Wikipedia and stays dropped. Appeal status of the Moss ruling was not found. The 2026-04-23 date shown for the Clearinghouse source is the partial final judgment date given on that page.
